archetype: ARCHETYPE 1: ORGANIC & EARTHY (Calm, Reassuring, Premium Learning)
emotional_tone: Warm, encouraging, low-pressure, dignified, and calm. Zero guilt, zero streak pressure, zero hyperactive gamification. Focus on restarting without catch-up debt.

fonts.heading: Outfit Variable
fonts.pairing_rationale: Outfit Variable provides an open, human, calming geometry for titles without feeling clinical or cold. DM Sans Variable offers effortless legibility and warm rhythm for narrative instructions. JetBrains Mono Variable renders clean, legible sample Python code.

entry_surfaces./session: distraction-free split workspace — exercise briefing with Make It Easier trigger left, dark-tinted code editor + hint drawer + keyword validation right

signature_interaction.name: Make It Easier
signature_interaction.purpose: Reduces friction when a learner feels stuck or intimidated. Swaps exercise into a simpler version without penalty, guilt, or condescending praise.
signature_interaction.ui_behavior: When clicked: 1) exercise description updates to shorter task, 2) starter code provides helpful scaffold, 3) a gentle banner appears: 'No judgment. Stepping stones build strong bridges. Try this simpler step.' 4) badge updates to 'Simplified Step' with a soft amber/coral badge, 5) validation keywords adjust dynamically.

pages_and_routes.description: Landing page introducing the low-pressure learning philosophy with clear CTA
Learner dashboard with active goal selector, session progress, and next recommended step
Interactive Python coding exercise with hint reveal, Make It Easier mode, and keyword checking
Log of completed sessions with ease-mode markers, timestamps, and calm reflections

sample_exercises.title: Printing Your Comeback Message
sample_exercises.task_standard: Write a Python script that defines a variable `message` with value 'Starting again today' and prints it using `print(message)`.
sample_exercises.starter_standard:
# Welcome back! Define your message and print it
message = "..."
sample_exercises.starter_easier:
# One simple line is all you need
print("Starting again today")
sample_exercises.hint: In Python, `print()` outputs text to the screen. You can pass a string or variable inside the parentheses.
sample_exercises.encouragement: Every long journey starts with a single executed line of code.

sample_exercises.title: Counting Your Micro-Wins
sample_exercises.task_standard: Create a list called `wins` with 3 items (e.g. 'showed up', 'opened editor', 'wrote code'). Print the length of the list using `len(wins)`.
sample_exercises.starter_standard:
# Record your small steps
wins = ["showed up", "opened editor", "wrote code"]
# Print how many wins you have
sample_exercises.task_easier: Print `len(['step 1', 'step 2'])` to see list length in action.
sample_exercises.starter_easier:
# Find the count of elements
wins = ["step 1", "step 2"]
print(len(wins))
sample_exercises.hint: The `len()` function returns the number of items inside any Python list or sequence.
sample_exercises.encouragement: Micro-wins compound faster than intense marathons.

sample_exercises.title: Building a Gentle Greeting Function
sample_exercises.task_standard: Define a function named `greet_learner(name)` that returns `f"Welcome back, {name}!"`. Call it with your name.
sample_exercises.starter_standard:
# Define your encouraging helper function
def greet_learner(name):
    return f"Welcome back, {name}!"

# Call the function below:
sample_exercises.task_easier: Fill in the return statement inside `def greet(name): return f'Hi {name}'`.
sample_exercises.hint: Functions use `def function_name(param):` and return values with the `return` keyword.
sample_exercises.encouragement: You're writing real, modular Python functions again. No rush.

motion_and_interactions.style: Subtle, smooth, zero aggressive bouncy effects
motion_and_interactions.transitions: transition-colors duration-200 ease-out, transition-opacity duration-150 ease-out
motion_and_interactions.easier_mode_transition: Gentle fade-in for the simplified task using Framer Motion or opacity transition

accessibility.wcag_compliance: WCAG AA minimum 4.5:1 text contrast for all body and muted copy
accessibility.test_attributes: All buttons, links, inputs, selects, code editors, tabs, and alerts MUST carry distinct `data-testid` attributes (e.g. data-testid='start-learning-btn', data-testid='make-it-easier-btn', data-testid='check-code-btn', data-testid='goal-switcher-select')

instructions_to_main_agent: Configure `frontend/src/index.css` with Outfit, DM Sans, and JetBrains Mono variable font imports and the warm off-white (#FAF8F5) background with deep navy (#1B2A4A) text tokens.
Mount 4 distinct pages in `App.tsx`: Home ('/'), Dashboard ('/dashboard'), Session ('/session/:sessionId?'), History ('/history').

Implement the FastAPI backend with MongoDB endpoints for getting goals, listing exercises, fetching session status, checking code (keyword verification), toggling 'Make It Easier', and recording completed sessions in DB for a single demo learner.
Include sample seed data in `backend/seed.py` for 3 distinct learning goals ('Python Basics', 'Pandas Micro-Tasks', 'HTTP & APIs') with pre-built standard & simplified exercises.
Display a visible 'Sample content' badge near exercise headers as instructed in problem statement.
Ensure 'Make It Easier' immediately swaps the code prompt and starter code with an encouraging banner and updates the active difficulty tag without guilt or exaggeration.
Ensure all interactive elements have explicit `data-testid` attributes for tests.
Verify frontend with `cd /app/frontend && yarn typecheck` and test API endpoints thoroughly.
